title: One step, one print line
idea: In lap 1, each plan step that shows something becomes one print line. Plan maps to code.

exercises.prompt: Your plan has 3 steps, each one 'show something'. How many print lines will the code have?
exercises.explanation: Each 'show' step becomes one print line. Three steps means three print lines.

exercises.prompt: Plan step: 'show the word Hello'. Which line of code matches it?
exercises.explanation: 'Show something' becomes print("..."). The plan step turns straight into one print line.

exercises.prompt: A plan step that says 'show X' usually becomes one print line in the code.
exercises.explanation: Yes! That is the neat part: each show-step maps to one print line. Plan, then code.

exercises.prompt: Plan: show Hi, then show Bye. Order the matching code lines.
exercises.explanation: The code lines follow the plan's order: Hi first, Bye second. Each step became one print line.

exercises.prompt: Plan: Step 1 show Good, Step 2 show Morning. What will the code show on screen?
options: Good then Morning on two lines
exercises.explanation: Two print lines each show their text on their own line: Good, then Morning.

exercises.prompt: Plan step: 'show the word Welcome'. Build the matching print line.
exercises.explanation: print, brackets, your text in quotes. One plan step became one tidy print line.

exercises.prompt: Plan: show Name, then show Age, then show Thanks. Order the code lines.
exercises.explanation: Three plan steps, three print lines, same order. Your plan became your program.

exercises.prompt: The order of your print lines should match the order of steps in your plan.
exercises.explanation: Yes. The code follows the plan top to bottom. Same steps, same order.

exercises.prompt: Plan: show Start, then show End. But the code is print("End") then print("Start"). What's wrong?
options: The code lines are in the wrong order
exercises.explanation: The plan said Start first, but the code shows End first. The lines are swapped — fix the order.

exercises.prompt: Plan step: 'show the word Done'. Write the full print line that matches it.
exercises.explanation: One plan step, one print line: print("Done"). You turned a plan into real code!
